body:
Reported by the maintainer on p23q.org/shopping after 2.1.0: the login page shows no cuneiform, and
https://p23q.org/shopping/tuppu-cuneiform.svg lands on the login page.

Cause: routes/webapp.py serves exactly two static things at the site root — /assets/<path> and
/favicon.svg — and everything else under the prefix falls into the SPA catch-all
(GET /<path:spa_path> -> index.html), whose router sends a logged-out visitor to login. The favicon
only works because it has an explicit route; T-225 put a second file in web/public/ and nothing
served it. The wheel smoke test checks that the favicon is served and not that any other root file is,
so it passed.

Fix the class: any regular file that exists at the root of the built web client (web_dist/, not
directories, no traversal — send_from_directory's safe join) is served as a cacheable asset before
the catch-all; a path that names no file still falls through to index.html. Server tests on both the
plain and the prefix mount: the svg is 200 image/svg+xml with the asset cache header, an unknown
file name still gets the SPA page. smoke-wheel.sh checks the cuneiform is served, so this cannot ship
silently again. docs/wire-contract.md's site-root table gains the row.

2.1.0 stays tagged; this supersedes it as 2.1.1.
title: A file at the root of the web bundle other than favicon.svg is swallowed by the SPA fallback — tuppu-cuneiform.svg redirects to login under a prefix mount
